summary: Same scene, same order, all facts, negations, causal links, the 'menen' irony in b015 and the four emphases intact; the narrator's hedge in b022 ('zo leek het') and the 'so that / even if / at least' chain are the closest of the three. All five comprehension questions answerable. One note.

comprehension.q: What does Michael say in reply to Petunia, and what does his tone give away?
comprehension.answer_from_nl: He says 'Dat meen je niet'; his tone gives him away: he is only too afraid — maybe she means it after all.

comprehension.q: According to Michael, how could what Petunia saw have been faked, and what name does he give to the trick of seeming to guess someone's thoughts?
comprehension.answer_from_nl: A trained stage magician (goochelaar) easily imitates such a thing; it only seems impossible — he taught Harry to bend spoons; if it seemed they could always guess your thoughts, that is called cold reading.

comprehension.q: What did Lily do to Petunia, and why did Lily do it?
comprehension.answer_from_nl: Lily made Petunia the way she is now (her slim figure); because Petunia begged her, for years.

comprehension.q: Why did Petunia beg Lily for years — what had she felt about Lily, and what did she want even though she could not have magic?
comprehension.answer_from_nl: Lily had always been prettier; Petunia had been mean to her because of that; then Lily got magic too. She begged Lily to use some of that magic on her so that she could also be pretty — if she couldn't have the magic, she could at least be pretty.

comprehension.q: What had Petunia told Lily and her husband about Michael, and why can't she just tell Michael what she saw?
comprehension.answer_from_nl: She had told them Michael was not allowed to know. She can't just tell him because then he will think she is— (unfinished).

findings.problem: 'verried hem' (gave him away) adds the idea that he was trying to hide the fear, where the English 'indicated' merely reports; the implication is already present in the contrast with 'Dat meen je niet', so the effect is unchanged.
findings.evidence: EN: 'His tone indicated that he was very much afraid that she was serious.' vs NL: 'Zijn toon verried hem: hij was maar al te bang. Misschien meende ze het toch.'
findings.required_fix: None required; keep. The 'meen je niet / meende ze het toch' echo carries the irony exactly.
